\section{Exact incidence certificate}
\label{app:incidence}

The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:central-surjectivity} is geometric and
does not depend on computation.  This appendix states an exact finite-matrix
cross-check.

On $B_d$, the numbers of vertices, positively oriented links, and plaquettes
are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:block-counts}
  3^d,qquad 2d\,3^{d-1},\qquad
  4\binom d2 3^{d-2},
\end{equation}
respectively.  Let $D$ be the unsigned plaquette--link incidence matrix.
Restrict $D$ to the $m$ rows incident to $e$ and delete the column of $e$.
Call the resulting matrix $C_d$.  If $o_p$ is the private opposite link of
$p$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:identity-minor}
  (C_d)_{p,o_{p'}}=\delta_{p,p'}.
\end{equation}
Thus $C_d$ has full row rank $m$ over every field.  For center signs in
$\SUtwo$, this is precisely surjectivity of the map
\[
  \mathbb F_2^{\,2d3^{d-1}-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^{\,m}.
\]

The supplementary program \texttt{supplement/verify\_incidence.py}
constructs the complete cubical complex using integer tuples, forms $C_d$,
computes its rank by exact Gaussian elimination over $\mathbb F_2$, verifies
the identity minor, and repeats the rank calculation after reversing row and
column order.  The shipped certificate covers $2\leq d\leq6$; these finite
checks illustrate the dimension-independent proof and are not logical inputs
to it.

For $d=4$, \eqref{eq:block-counts} gives $81$ vertices, $216$ links, and
$216$ plaquettes.  The selected full-degree link has $m=6$ incident
plaquettes, and the six private opposite columns give an exact $6\times6$
identity minor.
